newsitem.title: UK: Cable & Wireless up on broker comments.
newsitem.headline: Cable & Wireless up on broker comments.

text.p: Shares in Cable & Wireless (C&W) firmed 3p to 458p in early London trading on Monday, benefitting again from positive comments by Salomon Brothers, traders said.

On Thursday of last week, Salomon reinstated coverage of the stock with a "strong buy" recommendation, arguing that C&W's management was likely to solve the strategic problems facing it through an alliance.

Underpinning the attraction of the stock is the likelihood of higher than expected earnings growth than currently expected on the back of growth in Hong Kong Telecom, said Salomon analyst Andrew Harrington on Monday.

"A colleague in Hong Kong published a piece late last week on Hong Kong Telecom that focused on the fact that a mixture of cost control and a bounce back in China call volumes will result in its earnings growth in the next couple of years being about one to two percentage points higher than the market currently expects," said Harrington.
That should mean C&W shows earnings growth one to two percentage points ahead of expectation this year and three percent ahead of current consensus next year, said Harrington.

"Even if we're wrong on the strategic value argument there is higher than expected earnings growth and that will protect downside as an investor," he said. The company's Mercury One-2-One unit is also reported to be planning the launch of an aggressive marketing campaign next month.
"This is very welcome. One-2-One has a significant opportunity out there -- it just has to get its marketing act together," said Harrington.
